newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 29.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Jan 29.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Michael Bevan was named man of the match after helping Australia win in the Fourth Test and retain the Sir Frank Worrell Trophy. Bevan, who has a distinctive left-arm wrist spin, is now considered a front-line member of the Australian cricket team after he achieved a high batting score and 10 wickets against the West Indies. Page 20.

Australian cricket captain Mark Taylor says Australia's victory in the Fourth Test at Adelaide Oval has rendered the West Indies pace battery methods obsolete. He says Australia has won five and lost only two of the eight Tests against the West Indies in he last two years. Taylor credited the Australian performance to the ability of the batsman to overcome the relentless pace battery favoured by the West Indies. Page 20.

Officials of the Australian Soccer Players Association are preparing to go the Industrial Relations Commission to resolve a long-running pay dispute with the Australian soccer team, the Socceroos. The players are seeking 75 per cent of competition prize oney, a 20 per cent share of appearance fees and 10 per cent of television revenue. Page 19.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

Australia defeated the West Indies in the Fourth Test by an innings and 183 runs, after dismissing the visitors for 204. The win is being heralded as ending the era of fast bowling and batting power in cricket in favour of limited-overs bowling tactics. Page 42.

Australia's chances of winning the first round Davis Cup tie against France to be held at White City have been reduced by the withdrawal of Mark Philppoussis from the team. Philppoussis, ranked 26th in the world, was forced to withdraw to avoid aggravatig existing tendonitis injuries. Taking his place is Sandon Stolle, seeded 52nd. page 42.

Sixteen year old Brooke Townsend is being hailed as a possible new champion in women's world class swimming after she defeated Atlanta Olympian Stacey Gartrell in the 800 metre and 1,500 metre competitions at last week's NSW swimming championships. She hopes to be included in the 2000 Olympics swimming team. Page 41.
THE AGE

Australian cyclist Nick Gates won the opening stage of the Tour of Tasmania yesterday, earning his first points in this year's international competition. He is hoping to compete with the pro team of ZVVZ-Giant AIS in more than 130 races this year. The team is labouring under cuts made to its travel budget by the Australian Sports Commission. Page C8.

The tour to South Africa by the Australian cricket team is not expected to receive any free to air television, despite its billing as an unofficial world championship of cricket. Live coverage will be seen on Rupert Murdoch's Foxtel. Page C10.

Troy Corser is set to compete in the 500cc motorbike race at Phillip Island on October 5. Competing in the race is a change of career for Corser who has already had a magnificent career on superbikes winning the Australian title in 1993, the United Statestitle in 1994 and in 1996 becoming the youngest rider ever to win the world title. Page C8.
THE HERALD SUN

Australia's leading breaststroke coach Leigh Nugent is poised to lift Australia's backstroke standard which has been lagging in recent times. He is expected to apply for the position of national coach, and has already assembled a team he hopes to take to the 2000 Olympics. Page 70.

Australian Football League chief executive Wayne Jackson admitted yesterday that the game's traditional venue of Waverley Park is likely to become obsolete if the proposal to play matches at Docklands Victoria Stadium is carried through. He said the AFL nd individual teams had made no decision yet and were awaiting talks with consultant former AFL chief executive Ross Oakley. Page 78

Despite his team's loss in the Fourth Test to Australia, West Indies cricket captain Courtney Walsh is likely to retain his position. At 34, Walsh is approaching the end of a long and successful career but is still respected as one of the world's most consistent bowlers. Page 76.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

In a victory for Australian free to air television, Channel Seven is preparing to broadcast a Super League game live each Saturday night in the upcoming rugby competition. The first match to be shown will be the March 1 competition between the Queensland and ACT Brumbies. Previously Super 12 matches could only been seen on pay television channel Foxtel pay-TV. Page 70.

Australian Rugby League player Laurie Daley said yesterday that he believed that he would captain Australia at the Super League World Nines competition to be held in Townsville this weekend despite a persistent back injury. Australia will be playing New Zealand, Fiji and the United Sates among others. Page 62.

Australian golfer Brett Ogle is looking forward to this year's international golfing circuit. Having recovered from bad form and severe personal problems he will compete in the A$1.2 million Heineken Classic tomorrow. Ogle's form slipped dramatically last year when he slipped to 180th in the world rankings and was forced to quit the US Tour. Page 66.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
